_DESIGN_RULE: Ticks are the scarce currency, not margin - a tick burns every customer on the floor at once. So the big concession is TICK-cheap and MARGIN-expensive, and the small one is the reverse; a card better than another on both axes is a bug. No card may move appeal by a full appeal_step (5) for free, or it becomes a substitute for reading the customer and diagnosis stops paying. Every support card pays for its tick in exactly one of three currencies: your margin, their patience, or information.

cards.name: Explain the Product
cards.text: You walk them through it properly. The workhorse: costs nothing but the clock, and moves you slightly less than one place up their list.

cards.name: Offer a Discount
cards.text: You come down on it. The biggest move you can make in a single tick, and you pay for it out of your own pocket.

cards.name: Pad the Deal
cards.text: You quietly widen the spread. Play it BEFORE you start conceding - padding a deal you have already dragged to the line just pushes it back under.

cards.name: Small Talk
cards.text: Kids, weather, the drive over. Buys one person time; the tick still costs everyone else theirs.

cards.name: Read the Room
cards.text: You shut up and watch. Tells you their LINE - how high Appeal has to climb before they say yes - and which THIRD of the board they actually care about, before you spend a tick putting a product in front of them.

cards.name: Payment Framing
cards.text: 'That's eleven dollars a month.' Half the price of a discount for half the movement.

cards.name: Bundle It In
cards.text: 'Since we're already doing the other two...' Worth nothing on your first offer to someone and enormous on your fourth.

cards.name: Fearmonger
cards.text: You describe, vividly, what happens to people who skip it. It works. It also costs them a third of their afternoon.

cards.name: Hard Close
cards.text: You stop being pleasant about it. Two ticks off the whole floor, six off theirs, and it moves them further than anything else you own.
